instantiated_cells.justification: Lobbyists required to report must file bi-monthly reports by the 15th day after each bi-monthly reporting period, not annually.
The statute specifies bi-monthly reporting periods, so monthly reporting is not required.
Lobbyists who meet the threshold must file on a bi-monthly schedule, which is an 'other' frequency option.
Reporting is bi-monthly (six periods per year), not quarterly.
The only periodic spending report imposed on lobbyists in this article is bi-monthly, while semi-annual reports are filed by clients under § 1-j.
The statute uses fixed bi-monthly periods rather than a tri-annual schedule tied to a legislative calendar.

cell.value: Bi-monthly (Jan–Feb, Mar–Apr, May–Jun, Jul–Aug, Sep–Oct, Nov–Dec), due by the 15th day following each period.

instantiated_cells.justification: Section 1-h(a) enumerates six bi-monthly reporting periods and sets the due date as the fifteenth day after the period ends.
Lobbyists must report expenses and itemize those over $75 with amount, payee, and purpose, indicating itemized expense disclosure is required.
Lobbyists who meet the threshold must file bi-monthly reports (six times per year), which is not one of the standard annual/semiannual/quarterly/monthly options.
Each bi-monthly lobbyist report must include legislative bill numbers and other identifiers for executive orders, rules, and procurements on which the lobbyist lobbied.
The bi-monthly report must state the compensation paid or owed to the lobbyist by the client.
The required bi-monthly report lists subjects, bills, and the governmental body lobbied, but does not require disclosure of specific contacts or communications.
Section 1-h requires reporting compensation and expenses but does not require allocating expenditures per issue/bill.
Lobbyists must report 'a description of the general subject or subjects' on which they have lobbied.
The bi-monthly report requires disclosure of general subjects lobbied, satisfying the Tier 0 activity disclosure.

instantiated_cells.justification: Lobbyists must report lobbying 'expenses' (with limited exclusions) which encompasses expenditures such as gifts and entertainment as part of lobbying expenses.
The report must include 'any expenses expended, received or incurred' for lobbying, including non-salary expenses (with certain exclusions), covering indirect lobbying costs.
Lobbyists file bi-monthly reports that include the lobbyist and client names, lobbied issues/bill numbers, and compensation and expenses.
The bi-monthly report must contain the lobbyist's name, address, and telephone number.
Lobbyists must disclose bill numbers and other action identifiers (executive orders, rules, rates, procurements) on which they have lobbied.
The lobbyist bi-monthly report requires the client’s name, address, and phone but does not require stating whether the principal is public or private or describing its business nature.
The bi-monthly report must include the client's name, address, and telephone number.
Because each bi-monthly report is for the client on whose behalf the lobbyist is retained, it necessarily discloses the client/principal represented.
Lobbyists must report 'the legislative bill numbers of any bills' on which they have lobbied.
The report requires disclosure of 'compensation paid or owed to the lobbyist,' which is direct lobbying cost (compensation).
Lobbyists must report expenses expended/received/incurred for lobbying, which provides total expenditures toward lobbying (subject to statutory exclusions).
Lobbyists must file bi-monthly reports with itemized expenses over $75, issue/bill identifiers, and compensation, meeting the described itemized-report requirement.
Expenses over $75 must be detailed by amount, payee, and purpose (with beneficiary name in some cases), requiring itemized disclosure rather than only lump sums.
